sanskrit: ṛṣabhaṃ parvataṃ gatvā pāṇḍyeṣu surapūjitam vājapeyam avāpnoti nākapṛṣṭhe ca modate
english: Having gone to Mount Ṛṣabha in the Pāṇḍya country, worshipped by the gods, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice and rejoices on the back of heaven.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta kāverīṃ vṛtām apsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go to the Kāverī river, attended by hosts of Apsarases; bathing there, O king, a man obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: tatas tīre samudrasya kanyātīrtha upaspṛśet tatropaspṛśya rājendra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Then on the seashore one should touch the waters at the Kanyā-tīrtha; having touched the waters there, O lord of kings, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: atha gokarṇam āsādya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam samudramadhye rājendra sarvalokanamaskṛtam
english: Then having reached Gokarṇa, renowned in the three worlds, situated amid the ocean, O lord of kings, saluted by all the worlds—

sanskrit: yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ bhūtayakṣapiśācāś ca kiṃnarāḥ samahoragāḥ
english: —where gods headed by Brahmā, sages rich in austerities, Bhūtas, Yakṣas, Piśācas, Kiṃnaras, and great serpents—

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇagandharvā mānuṣāḥ pannagās tathā saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā upāsanta umāpatim
english: —Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, men, Nāgas, rivers, oceans, and mountains all worship the Lord of Umā—

sanskrit: tatreśānaṃ samabhyarcya trirātropoṣito naraḥ daśāśvamedham āpnoti gāṇapatyaṃ ca vindati uṣya dvādaśarātraṃ tu kṛtātmā bhavate naraḥ
english: —there, having duly worshipped Īśāna with a three-night fast, a man obtains the merit of ten Aśvamedha sacrifices and attains membership in Gaṇeśa's host; having dwelt there for twelve nights, a man becomes purified in soul.

sanskrit: tata eva tu gāyatryāḥ sthānaṃ trailokyaviśrutam trirātram uṣitas tatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Right there too is the abode of Gāyatrī, renowned in the three worlds; dwelling there for three nights one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: nidarśanaṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ narādhipa gāyatrīṃ paṭhate yas tu yonisaṃkarajas tathā gāthā vā gītikā vāpi tasya saṃpadyate nṛpa
english: There is even a visible proof for Brāhmaṇas, O lord of men: he who recites the Gāyatrī — even one born of a mixed union — or sings a hymn or a song there, to him it becomes fully effective, O king.

sanskrit: saṃvartasya tu viprarṣer vāpīm āsādya durlabhām rūpasya bhāgī bhavati subhagaś caiva jāyate
english: Having reached the difficult-to-find well of the sage Saṃvarta, one becomes endowed with beauty and is born fortunate.

sanskrit: tato veṇṇāṃ samāsādya tarpayet pitṛdevatāḥ mayūrahaṃsasaṃyuktaṃ vimānaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: Then having reached the Veṇṇā river, one should satisfy the ancestors and gods; a man thereby obtains a celestial chariot adorned with peacocks and swans.

sanskrit: tato godāvarīṃ prāpya nityaṃ siddhaniṣevitam gavāmayam avāpnoti vāsuker lokam āpnuyāt
english: Then having reached the Godāvarī, ever frequented by Siddhas, one attains the merit of the Gavāmayana sacrifice and reaches the world of Vāsuki.

sanskrit: veṇṇāyāḥ saṃgame snātvā vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet varadāsaṃgame snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Bathing at the confluence of the Veṇṇā one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice; bathing at the confluence of the Varadā one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: brahmasthānaṃ samāsādya trirātram uṣito naraḥ gosahasraphalaṃ vindet svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Having reached Brahmasthāna, a man who has dwelt there for three nights obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows and goes to the world of heaven.

sanskrit: kuśaplavanam āsādya brahmacārī samāhitaḥ trirātram uṣitaḥ snātvā aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Having reached Kuśaplavana, a celibate with concentrated mind, having dwelt and bathed there for three nights, obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato devahrade ramye kṛṣṇaveṇṇājalodbhave jātimātrahrade caiva tathā kanyāśrame nṛpa
english: Then at the beautiful Devahrada, born from the waters of the Kṛṣṇa-Veṇṇā, and also at the Jātimātra lake, and at the Kanyāśrama, O king—

sanskrit: yatra kratuśatair iṣṭvā devarājo divaṃ gataḥ agniṣṭomaśataṃ vinded gamanād eva bhārata
english: —where the king of gods went to heaven having offered a hundred sacrifices, one obtains the merit of a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices merely by going there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sarvadevahrade snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet jātimātrahrade snātvā bhavej jātismaro naraḥ
english: Bathing in the Sarvadevahrada one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows; bathing in the Jātimātra lake a man becomes one who remembers his former births.

sanskrit: tato 'vāpya mahāpuṇyāṃ payoṣṇīṃ saritāṃ varām pitṛdevārcanarato gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then having reached the greatly holy Payoṣṇī, best of rivers, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods, one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: daṇḍakāraṇyam āsādya mahārāja upaspṛśet gosahasraphalaṃ tatra snātamātrasya bhārata
english: Having reached the Daṇḍaka forest, O great king, and touching the sacred waters, one who merely bathes there obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śarabhaṅgāśramaṃ gatvā śukasya ca mahātmanaḥ na durgatim avāpnoti punāti ca kulaṃ naraḥ
english: Having gone to the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga and of the great-souled Śuka, a man does not attain an evil state and he purifies his lineage.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpārakaṃ gacchej jāmadagnyaniṣevitam rāmatīrthe naraḥ snātvā vindyād bahu suvarṇakam
english: Then one should go to Śūrpāraka, frequented by the son of Jamadagni; a man bathing at the Rāma-tīrtha there obtains abundant gold.

sanskrit: saptagodāvare snātvā niyato niyatāśanaḥ mahat puṇyam avāpnoti devalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Bathing at the Sapta-Godāvarī, disciplined and with regulated food, one attains great merit and goes to the world of the gods.

sanskrit: tato devapathaṃ gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ devasatrasya yat puṇyaṃ tad avāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Then one should go to Devapatha, disciplined with regulated food; a human being obtains the merit of a Devasatra sacrifice.

sanskrit: tuṅgakāraṇyam āsādya brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ vedān adhyāpayat tatra ṛṣiḥ sārasvataḥ purā
english: Having reached the Tuṅgaka forest, a celibate with controlled senses — there the sage Sārasvata taught the Vedas in former times.

sanskrit: tatra vedān pranaṣṭāṃs tu muner aṅgirasaḥ sutaḥ upaviṣṭo maharṣīṇām uttarīyeṣu bhārata
english: There the Vedas that had been lost — the son of the sage Aṅgiras — sitting upon the upper garments of the great sages, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: oṃkāreṇa yathānyāyaṃ samyag uccāritena ca yena yat pūrvam abhyastaṃ tat tasya samupasthitam
english: —through the Oṃkāra properly and correctly uttered, whatever each sage had formerly studied came back present to him.

sanskrit: ṛṣayas tatra devāś ca varuṇo 'gniḥ prajāpatiḥ harir nārāyaṇo devo mahādevas tathaiva ca
english: There sages and gods — Varuṇa, Agni, Prajāpati, Lord Hari-Nārāyaṇa, Mahādeva as well—

sanskrit: pitāmahaś ca bhagavān devaiḥ saha mahādyutiḥ bhṛguṃ niyojayām āsa yājanārthe mahādyutim
english: —and the blessed Grandfather of great splendour, together with the gods, appointed the great-resplendent Bhṛgu for the purpose of performing the sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa cakre bhagavān ṛṣīṇāṃ vidhivat tadā sarveṣāṃ punar ādhānaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then the blessed one duly performed for all those sages once more the sacred fire-installation, through the rites prescribed by the scriptures.

sanskrit: ājyabhāgena vai tatra tarpitās tu yathāvidhi devās tribhuvaṇaṃ yātā ṛṣayaś ca yathāsukham
english: There indeed the gods, duly satisfied with their shares of clarified butter, went to the three worlds, and the sages departed in happiness.

sanskrit: tad araṇyaṃ praviṣṭasya tuṅgakaṃ rājasattama pāpaṃ praṇaśyate sarvaṃ striyo vā puruṣasya vā
english: All sin of one who has entered that forest Tuṅgaka, O best of kings, is destroyed — whether of a woman or a man.

sanskrit: tatra māsaṃ vased dhīro niyato niyatāśanaḥ brahmalokaṃ vrajed rājan punīte ca kulaṃ naraḥ
english: A wise man who dwells there for a month, disciplined and with regulated food, goes to the world of Brahmā, O king, and the man purifies his lineage.

sanskrit: medhāvikaṃ samāsādya pitṝn devāṃś ca tarpayet agniṣṭomam avāpnoti smṛtiṃ medhāṃ ca vindati
english: Having reached Medhāvika and satisfying the ancestors and gods, one attains the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and gains memory and intelligence.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālaṃjaraṃ gatvā parvataṃ lokaviśrutam tatra devahrade snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then having gone to Mount Kālaṃjara, renowned in the world, bathing there in the Devahrada, one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ sādhayet tatra girau kālaṃjare nṛpa svargaloke mahīyeta naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: One should discipline oneself there on Mount Kālaṃjara, O king; a man would be honoured in the world of heaven — there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit: tato girivaraśreṣṭhe citrakūṭe viśāṃ pate mandākinīṃ samāsādya nadīṃ pāpapramocanīm
english: Then on Citrakūṭa, best of excellent mountains, O lord of peoples, having reached the Mandākinī river that removes sins—

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇaḥ pitṛdevārcane rataḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti gatiṃ ca paramāṃ vrajet
english: —one who performs ablutions there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods, obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra bhartṛsthānam anuttamam yatra devo mahāseno nityaṃ saṃnihito nṛpaḥ
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the unequalled abode of the Lord, where the god Mahāsena is ever present, O king.

sanskrit: pumāṃs tatra naraśreṣṭha gamanād eva sidhyati koṭitīrthe naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: A man, O best of men, succeeds there merely by going; bathing at Koṭi-tīrtha, a man obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya jyeṣṭhasthānaṃ vrajen naraḥ abhigamya mahādevaṃ virājati yathā śaśī
english: Having circumambulated in the rightward direction, a man should go to the Jyeṣṭhāsthāna; having visited Mahādeva there, he shines like the moon.

sanskrit: tatra kūpo mahārāja viśruto bharatarṣabha samudrās tatra catvāro nivasanti yudhiṣṭhira
english: There is a renowned well there, O great king, O bull of the Bharatas; four oceans dwell there, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tatropaspṛśya rājendra kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam niyatātmā naraḥ pūto gaccheta paramāṃ gatim
english: Having touched the sacred waters there, O lord of kings, and having performed the circumambulation, a man of controlled soul, purified, goes to the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gacchet kuruśreṣṭha śṛṅgaverapuraṃ mahat yatra tīrṇo mahārāja rāmo dāśarathiḥ purā
english: Then one should go, O best of Kurus, to the great city of Śṛṅgavera, where Rāma son of Daśaratha once crossed the river, O great king.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāṃ tu naraḥ snātvā brahmacārī samāhitaḥ vidhūtapāpmā bhavati vājapeyaṃ ca vindati
english: A celibate man with concentrated mind, bathing in the Gaṅgā there, becomes free of sin and obtains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: abhigamya mahādevam abhyarcya ca narādhipa pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya gāṇapatyam avāpnuyāt
english: Having visited and duly worshipped Mahādeva, O lord of men, and having circumambulated, one attains membership in the host of Gaṇa.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra prayāgam ṛṣisaṃstutam yatra brahmādayo devā diśaś ca sadigīśvarāḥ
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to Prayāga, praised by the sages, where gods headed by Brahmā, the directions with their lords—

sanskrit: lokapālāś ca sādhyāś ca nairṛtāḥ pitaras tathā sanatkumārapramukhās tathaiva paramarṣayaḥ
english: —guardians of the worlds, Sādhyas, Nairṛtas, the ancestors, the great sages headed by Sanatkumāra—

sanskrit: aṅgiraḥpramukhāś caiva tathā brahmarṣayo 'pare tathā nāgāḥ suparṇāś ca siddhāś cakracarās tathā
english: —and the Brahma-sages headed by Aṅgiras, other sages, and Nāgas, Suparṇas, Siddhas, and those who move in circles—

sanskrit: saritaḥ sāgarāś caiva gandharvāpsarasas tathā hariś ca bhagavān āste prajāpatipuraskṛtaḥ
english: —rivers, oceans, Gandharvas, and Apsarases dwell, and the blessed Lord Hari abides there, honored by Prajāpati.

sanskrit: tatra trīṇy agnikuṇḍāni yeṣāṃ madhye ca jāhnavī prayāgād abhiniṣkrāntā sarvatīrthasamīkṣayā
english: There are three fire-altars there, in the midst of which the Jāhnavī, departing from Prayāga, is regarded as the foremost of all tīrthas.

sanskrit: tapanasya sutā tatra triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā yamunā gaṅgayā sārdhaṃ saṃgatā lokapāvanī
english: There the daughter of the Sun, renowned in the three worlds, Yamunā, meets with the Gaṅgā, she who purifies the worlds.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyamunayor madhyaṃ pṛthivyā jaghanaṃ smṛtam prayāgaṃ jaghanasyāntam upastham ṛṣayo viduḥ
english: The confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā is regarded as the lap of the earth; Prayāga the sages know as the front part of that lap, its innermost core.

sanskrit: prayāgaṃ sapratiṣṭhānaṃ kambalāśvatarau tathā tīrthaṃ bhogavatī caiva vedī proktā prajāpateḥ
english: Prayāga along with Pratiṣṭhāna, Kambala and Aśvatara, the tīrtha of Bhogavatī — these are declared the sacrificial altar of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: tatra vedāś ca yajñāś ca mūrtimanto yudhiṣṭhira prajāpatim upāsante ṛṣayaś ca mahāvratāḥ yajante kratubhir devās tathā cakracarā nṛpa
english: There the Vedas and sacrifices in embodied form, O Yudhiṣṭhira, attend upon Prajāpati; the sages of great vows also attend there; the gods and those who move in circles worship with sacred rites, O king.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ nāsti triṣu lokeṣu bhārata prayāgaḥ sarvatīrthebhyaḥ prabhavaty adhikaṃ vibho
english: There is nothing more holy than that in the three worlds, O Bhārata; Prayāga surpasses all other tīrthas, O lord.

sanskrit: śravaṇāt tasya tīrthasya nāmasaṃkīrtanād api mṛttikālambhanād vāpi naraḥ pāpāt pramucyate
english: By merely hearing of that tīrtha, even by the chanting of its name, or even by taking hold of its clay, a man is freed from sin.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame saṃśitavrataḥ puṇyaṃ sa phalam āpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ
english: One who performs ablutions at the confluence there, firm in vow, obtains the holy fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: eṣā yajanabhūmir hi devānām api satkṛtā tatra dattaṃ sūkṣmam api mahad bhavati bhārata
english: For this is the sacrificial ground honoured even by the gods; whatever is given there, even if small, becomes great, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na vedavacanāt tāta na lokavacanād api matir utkramaṇīyā te prayāgamaraṇaṃ prati
english: Neither by the word of the Veda, dear one, nor by the word of the world either, should your mind be turned away from dying at Prayāga.

sanskrit: daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭtyas tathāparāḥ yeṣāṃ sāṃnidhyam atraiva kīrtitaṃ kurunandana
english: Ten thousand tīrthas and sixty crore more — their proximity here at Prayāga alone is celebrated, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: cāturvede ca yat puṇyaṃ satyavādiṣu caiva yat snāta eva tadāpnoti gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame
english: The merit that resides in the four Vedas and the merit that resides in those who speak the truth — all that a bather obtains at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

sanskrit: tatra bhogavatī nāma vāsukes tīrtham uttamam tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt so 'śvamedham avāpnuyāt
english: There is the excellent tīrtha of Vāsuki named Bhogavatī; one who performs ablutions there obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatra haṃsaprapatanaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam daśāśvamedhikaṃ caiva gaṅgāyāṃ kurunandana
english: There is the tīrtha of Haṃsaprapatana, renowned in the three worlds, and also the Daśāśvamedhika on the Gaṅgā, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yatra gaṅgā mahārāja sa deśas tat tapovanam siddhakṣetraṃ tu taj jñeyaṃ gaṅgātīrasamāśritam
english: Wherever the Gaṅgā flows, O great king, that region is a forest of austerities; it should be known as a holy field of the Siddhas, situated on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: idaṃ satyaṃ dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnām ātmajasya ca suhṛdāṃ ca japet karṇe śiṣyasyānugatasya ca
english: This truth one should whisper in the ear of twice-born persons, the virtuous, one's own sons, one's friends, and one's devoted pupils.

sanskrit: idaṃ dharmyam idaṃ puṇyam idaṃ medhyam idaṃ sukham idaṃ svargyam idaṃ ramyam idaṃ pāvanam uttamam
english: This is righteous, this is holy, this is auspicious, this is joyful, this leads to heaven, this is delightful, this is the highest purifier.

sanskrit: maharṣīṇām idaṃ guhyaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam adhītya dvijamadhye ca nirmalatvam avāpnuyāt
english: This is the secret of the great sages, the remover of all sin; having studied it, among twice-born men one attains purity.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ tīrthapuṇyaṃ sadā śuciḥ jātīḥ sa smarate bahvīr nākapṛṣṭhe ca modate
english: Whoever constantly hears this merit of the tīrthas, always pure, remembers many former births and rejoices on the back of heaven.

sanskrit: gamyāny api ca tīrthāni kīrtitāny agamāni ca manasā tāni gaccheta sarvatīrthasamīkṣayā
english: The tīrthas that can be reached as well as those that have been named as unreachable — one should go to them all in mind, with a view to visiting all tīrthas.

sanskrit: etāni vasubhiḥ sādhyair ādityair marudaśvibhiḥ ṛṣibhir devakalpaiś ca śritāni sukṛtaiṣibhiḥ
english: These tīrthas have been resorted to by the Vasus, Sādhyas, Ādityas, Maruts, Aśvins, sages equal to gods, and those who seek merit.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvam api kauravya vidhinānena suvrata vraja tīrthāni niyataḥ puṇyaṃ puṇyena vardhate
english: Thus you too, O Kauravya, O one of excellent vows, should visit the tīrthas according to this rule, in a disciplined manner; merit grows through merit.

sanskrit: bhāvitaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ pūrvam āstikyāc chrutidarśanāt prāpyante tāni tīrthāni sadbhiḥ śiṣṭānudarśibhiḥ
english: Through causes cultivated in former lives, through faith, and through the guidance of the Vedas, those tīrthas are reached by the virtuous who follow the example of the learned.

sanskrit: nāvrato nākṛtātmā ca nāśucir na ca taskaraḥ snāti tīrtheṣu kauravya na ca vakramatir naraḥ
english: One without vows, one who has not disciplined himself, the impure, a thief — they do not truly bathe at tīrthas, O Kauravya, nor does a man of crooked conduct.

sanskrit: tvayā tu samyagvṛttena nityaṃ dharmārthadarśinā pitaras tāritās tāta sarve ca prapitāmahāḥ
english: But by you, of proper conduct, always seeing the aims of righteousness, your ancestors have been ferried across, dear one, and all your great-grandfathers as well.

sanskrit: pitāmahapurogāś ca devāḥ sarṣigaṇā nṛpa tava dharmeṇa dharmajña nityam evābhitoṣitāḥ
english: The gods headed by the Grandfather, together with the host of sages, O king, are ever pleased, O knower of righteousness, by your righteousness.

sanskrit: avāpsyasi ca lokān vai vasūnāṃ vāsavopama kīrtiṃ ca mahatīṃ bhīṣma prāpsyase bhuvi śāśvatīm
english: You shall attain the worlds of the Vasus, O one like Vāsava, and great fame, O Bhīṣma, you shall obtain upon earth that is eternal.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evam uktvābhyanujñāpya pulastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ prītaḥ prītena manasā tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Nārada said: Having thus spoken and having taken leave, the blessed sage Pulastya, pleased and with a joyful mind, vanished there on the spot.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaś ca kuruśārdūla śāstratattvārthadarśivān pulastyavacanāc caiva pṛthivīm anucakrame
english: And Bhīṣma, O tiger among Kurus, who beheld the true import of the scriptures, following the words of Pulastya, traversed the earth.

sanskrit: anena vidhinā yas tu pṛthivīṃ saṃcariṣyati aśvamedhaśatasyāgryaṃ phalaṃ pretya sa bhokṣyate
english: One who shall traverse the earth according to this rule shall, after death, enjoy the foremost fruit of a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices.
